raw_text: NEW DELHI (Reuters) — India deployed thousands of troops and imposed a shoot-on-sight curfew in the northeastern state of Manipur on Thursday after ethnic clashes killed at least 60 people and displaced more than 23,000 in two days of violence. The conflict between the Meitei and Kuki communities was triggered by a contentious court order on tribal status. Witnesses described mobs armed with guns looted from police stations attacking homes and places of worship. Columns of smoke rose over Imphal as burned-out vehicles and destroyed buildings lined the main highway. The government cut internet and mobile services across the state. India's Home Minister said the situation was being monitored at the highest levels.
